units.zh: 王周，魏州人。
units.en: Wang Zhou was a native of Weizhou.
units.literal: Wang Zhou was a man of Weizhou.

units.zh: 少勇健，從軍事唐莊宗、明宗，稍遷裨校，以戰功累歷郡守。
units.en: As a young man he was vigorous and daring. He served under Emperors Zhuangzong and Mingzong of Tang, rose step by step through the officer ranks, and with repeated victories held one prefectural post after another.
units.literal: In youth he was brave and strong; he followed the armies in service to Tang Emperors Zhuangzong and Mingzong, was gradually promoted to staff officer, and through battle achievements successively held prefectural governorships.

units.zh: 晉天福初，範延光叛於魏州，周從楊光遠攻降之，安重榮以鎮州叛，從杜重威討平之，以功授貝州節度使。
units.en: Early in the Jin Tianfu reign, Fan Yanguang rebelled in Weizhou and Zhou joined Yang Guangyuan in the campaign that brought him down. When An Chongrong rose in Zhenzhou, Zhou followed Du Chongwei to crush that revolt and, for these services, was made military commissioner of Beizhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Jin Tianfu era, Fan Yanguang rebelled at Weizhou; Zhou followed Yang Guangyuan to attack and subdue him. An Chongrong rebelled with Zhenzhou; he followed Du Chongwei to suppress and pacify him, and for merit was appointed military commissioner of Beizhou.

units.zh: 歲餘，移鎮涇州。
units.en: A little over a year later he was reassigned to Jingzhou.
units.literal: After more than a year, he was transferred to garrison Jingzhou.

units.zh: 先是，前帥張彥澤在任苛虐，部民逃者五千餘戶，及下車，革前弊二十餘事，逃民歸復，賜詔褒美。
units.en: His predecessor Zhang Yanzhe had ruled with harsh cruelty, and more than five thousand households had fled the prefecture. When Zhou arrived he abolished more than twenty longstanding abuses, the refugees came back, and the court issued an edict commending his administration.
units.literal: Previously the former commander Zhang Yanzhe had been harsh and cruel in office; more than five thousand households of the district had fled. When Zhou took up his post, he reformed more than twenty abuses of the past, the fugitive people returned, and an edict was bestowed praising him.

units.zh: 後歷鄧、陜二鎮。
units.en: He later served in succession at Dengzhou and Shaanzhou.
units.literal: Later he successively held the two garrisons of Deng and Shaan.

units.zh: 陽城之役，周時為定州節度使，大軍往來，供饋無闕，未幾，遷鎮州節度使。
units.en: During the battle at Yangcheng he was military commissioner of Dingzhou and kept the armies supplied without fail as they marched back and forth. Soon afterward he was moved to Zhenzhou.
units.literal: In the Yangcheng campaign, Zhou was then military commissioner of Dingzhou; as the great army came and went, provisions were supplied without shortage. Before long he was transferred to military commissioner of Zhenzhou.

units.zh: 周稟性寬惠，人庶便之。
units.en: By nature Zhou was lenient and benevolent, and the common people flourished under him.
units.literal: Zhou's nature was generous and kind; the people found him convenient.

units.zh: 開運末，杜重威降於契丹，引契丹主臨城諭之。
units.en: Late in the Kaiyun era Du Chongwei surrendered to the Khitan and brought the Khitan emperor to the walls to urge the garrison to submit.
units.literal: At the end of Kaiyun, Du Chongwei surrendered to the Khitan; he brought the Khitan ruler to the city to announce and persuade them.

units.zh: 周泣曰：「受國重恩，不能死戰，而以兵降，何面南行見人主與士大夫乎？」
units.en: Zhou wept and said, "The state has shown me great favor, yet I could not die fighting and instead surrendered my troops. How can I face south and go before the emperor and the court?"
units.literal: Zhou wept and said: "Having received the state's heavy grace, I could not die in battle but instead surrender with troops—what face have I to go south and see the sovereign and the scholar-officials?"

units.zh: 乃痛飲欲引決，家人止之。
units.en: He drank deeply, intending to kill himself, but his household stopped him.
units.literal: He then drank heavily intending to take his own life, but his family restrained him.

units.zh: 事不獲已，乃見契丹主，授鄧州節度使、檢校太師。
units.en: When there was no alternative he went before the Khitan emperor and was given the posts of military commissioner of Dengzhou and honorary Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: The matter could not be helped; he then saw the Khitan ruler and was appointed military commissioner of Dengzhou and honorary Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 高祖定天下，移鎮徐州，加同平章事。
units.en: After Gaozu secured the empire, Zhou was reassigned to Xuzhou and made a co-director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: When Gaozu settled the realm, Zhou was transferred to garrison Xuzhou and given the additional title of Tongping Zhangshi.

units.zh: 乾祐元年二月，以疾卒於鎮，輟視朝二日，贈中書令。
units.en: In the second month of Qianyou 1 he died of illness in office. The court suspended audiences for two days and posthumously appointed him Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: In the second month of the first year of Qianyou he died of illness at his post; court audiences were suspended for two days, and he was posthumously made Zhongshu Ling.

units.zh: 周性寬恕，不忤物情。
units.en: Zhou was forbearing by nature and never set himself against popular sentiment.
units.literal: Zhou's disposition was forgiving and did not go against people's feelings.

units.zh: 初刺信都，州城西橋敗，覆民租車，周曰：「橋梁不飭，刺史之過也。」
units.en: Early in his tenure at Xindu the west bridge of the city collapsed and overturned carts carrying the people's grain tax. Zhou said, "When bridges are left in disrepair, the fault lies with the prefect."
units.literal: When he first governed Xindu, the west bridge of the prefectural city collapsed and overturned the people's grain-tax carts. Zhou said: "Bridges not maintained are the prefect's fault."

units.zh: 乃還其所沈粟，出私財以修之，民庶悅焉。
units.en: He returned the grain that had been lost, paid for repairs out of his own purse, and the people rejoiced.
units.literal: He then returned the grain that had sunk, spent private funds to repair it, and the people were pleased.

units.zh: 劉審交，字求益，幽州文安人也。
units.en: Liu Shenjiao, courtesy name Qiuyi, was a native of Wen'an in Youzhou.
units.literal: Liu Shenjiao, style name Qiuyi, was a man of Wen'an in Youzhou.

units.zh: 祖海，父師遂。
units.en: His grandfather was named Hai and his father Shisui.
units.literal: His grandfather was Hai; his father was Shisui.

units.zh: 審交少讀書，尤精吏道，起家署北平主簿，轉興唐令，本府召補牙職。
units.en: Shenjiao studied from an early age and excelled above all in administrative practice. He entered service as registrar of Beiping, became magistrate of Xingtang, and was then recalled to headquarters as a staff officer.
units.literal: Shenjiao in youth studied books and was especially skilled in the ways of clerical administration. He began his career as registrar of Beiping, was transferred to magistrate of Xingtang, and the headquarters summoned him to fill a staff post.

units.zh: 劉守光之僭號，偽署兵部尚書，燕亡，歸於太原。
units.en: When Liu Shouguang declared himself emperor, Shenjiao was given the bogus title of Minister of War. After Yan fell he made his way back to Taiyuan.
units.literal: When Liu Shouguang usurped the title, he was falsely appointed Minister of War; when Yan perished, he returned to Taiyuan.

units.zh: 莊宗知之，用為諸府從事。
units.en: Zhuangzong heard of him and put him to work as an aide in several headquarters.
units.literal: Zhuangzong learned of him and employed him as an aide in various offices.

units.zh: 同光初，趙德鈞鎮幽州，朝廷以內官馬紹宏為北面轉運使，辟審交為判官。
units.en: Early in the Tongguang era Zhao Dejun held Youzhou. The court sent the eunuch Ma Shohong as northern transport commissioner, and Shenjiao joined his staff as chief aide.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang, Zhao Dejun garrisoned Youzhou; the court appointed the inner attendant Ma Shohong as northern transport commissioner and recruited Shenjiao as his aide.

units.zh: 王都據定州叛，朝廷命王晏球進討，以審交為轉運供軍使，王都平，以勞授遼州刺史。
units.en: When Wang Du rebelled from Dingzhou the court sent Wang Yanqiu against him with Shenjiao as transport and supply officer. After Wang Du was subdued, Shenjiao was rewarded with the prefecture of Liaozhou.
units.literal: Wang Du held Dingzhou and rebelled; the court ordered Wang Yanqiu to advance and attack, appointing Shenjiao transport and army-supply commissioner. When Wang Du was pacified, for his labor he was made prefect of Liaozhou.

units.zh: 明年，復為北面供軍轉運使，改磁州刺史，以母年高，去官就養。
units.en: The following year he again served as northern supply transport commissioner, then became prefect of Cizhou. When his mother grew old he resigned to care for her at home.
units.literal: The next year he again became northern army-supply transport commissioner, was changed to prefect of Cizhou, and because his mother was advanced in years left office to go and support her.

units.zh: 及丁內艱，毀瘠過禮，服闋，不出累年。
units.en: After her death he mourned so severely that he wasted beyond what ritual required, and when the mourning period ended he stayed in seclusion for years.
units.literal: When he entered mourning for his mother he wasted away beyond the rites; when mourning ended he did not go out for many years.

units.zh: 晉高祖踐阼，範延光以魏州叛，命楊光遠以總兵討之，復召審交為供饋使。
units.en: When Jin Gaozu took the throne, Fan Yanguang rebelled in Weizhou. Yang Guangyuan was placed in overall command of the punitive force, and Shenjiao was called back as supply commissioner.
units.literal: When Jin Gaozu ascended the throne, Fan Yanguang rebelled with Weizhou; Yang Guangyuan was ordered to take overall command to suppress him, and Shenjiao was again summoned as supply commissioner.

units.zh: 鄴中平，命審交為三司使，授右衛大將軍。
units.en: After Ye was pacified he was made commissioner of the Three Departments and appointed Grand General of the Right Guards.
units.literal: When Yezhong was pacified, Shenjiao was ordered to be commissioner of the Three Departments and given the post of Grand General of the Right Guards.

units.zh: 六年夏，出為陳州防禦使，歲餘，移襄州防禦使。
units.en: In the summer of the sixth year he became defense commissioner of Chenzhou, and a little over a year later was moved to Xiangzhou.
units.literal: In the summer of the sixth year he went out as defense commissioner of Chenzhou; after more than a year he was transferred to defense commissioner of Xiangzhou.

units.zh: 審交治襄、漢，撫綏有術，民庶懷之。
units.en: In Xiang and Han he governed with a sure hand at reassurance and settlement, and the people held him in affection.
units.literal: Shenjiao governed Xiang and Han with skill in soothing and binding; the people cherished him.

units.zh: 青州楊光遠平，降平盧軍為防禦州，復用審交為防禦使，累官至檢校太傅。
units.en: After Yang Guangyuan of Qingzhou was subdued, Pinglu was reduced to a defense command and Shenjiao was sent back as its commissioner. He eventually rose to honorary Grand Tutor.
units.literal: When Yang Guangyuan of Qingzhou was pacified, Pinglu Army was reduced to a defense prefecture; Shenjiao was again used as defense commissioner and rose in office to honorary Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 時用軍之後，審交矜恤撫理，雕弊復蘇。
units.en: In the aftermath of war he nursed the wounded region back to health with compassionate care, and a devastated land began to recover.
units.literal: At a time after military use, Shenjiao showed compassion in soothing and ordering; the exhausted revived.

units.zh: 契丹破晉，審交以代歸，蕭翰在都，復用為三司使。
units.en: When the Khitan overthrew Jin, Shenjiao came back from Dai. Xiao Han held the capital and again appointed him commissioner of the Three Departments.
units.literal: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, Shenjiao returned from Dai; Xiao Han was in the capital and again employed him as commissioner of the Three Departments.

units.zh: 翰歸蕃，李從益在汴州，召高行周、武行德將委以軍事，皆不受命。
units.en: After Han withdrew to the steppe, Li Congyi was at Bianzhou and summoned Gao Xingzhou and Wu Xingde to take command of the armies, but neither would accept.
units.literal: When Han returned to the barbarians, Li Congyi was at Bianzhou; he summoned the generals Gao Xingzhou and Wu Xingde intending to entrust them with military affairs, but none accepted the commission.

units.zh: 尋聞高祖起義於太原，史宏肇在澤潞，都人大懼。
units.en: Word soon came that Gaozu had risen in Taiyuan while Shi Hongzhao held Ze and Lu, and the people of the capital were seized with fear.
units.literal: Soon they heard that Gaozu had raised the righteous army at Taiyuan; Shi Hongzhao was at Ze and Lu, and the people of the capital were greatly afraid.

units.zh: 時有燕軍千人守捉諸門，李從益母王淑妃詢於文武臣僚曰：「予子母在洛，孤危自處，一旦為蕭翰所逼，致令及此。
units.en: A thousand Yan troops then held the gates. Li Congyi's mother, Lady Wang Shufei, asked the civil and military officials, "My son and I were left alone and vulnerable in Luoyang, and now, driven to this pass by Xiao Han, we stand in grave danger.
units.literal: At the time a thousand Yan troops guarded the gates. Li Congyi's mother, Consort Wang Shufei, inquired of civil and military officials: "My son and I are in Luoyang, isolated and in peril on our own; suddenly pressed by Xiao Han, matters have come to this.

units.zh: 但遣人迎請太原，勿以予子母為事。」
units.en: Send envoys to welcome the forces from Taiyuan and do not trouble yourselves over my son and me."
units.literal: Only send men to welcome and invite Taiyuan; do not make an issue of my son and me."

units.zh: 或曰：「收拾諸處守營兵士與燕軍，足以把城，以俟河北救應可也。」
units.en: Others urged, "Rally the garrison troops from every post together with the Yan forces—we can hold the city until help arrives from Hebei."
units.literal: Someone said: "Gather the garrison soldiers from the various posts together with the Yan army—enough to hold the city and await rescue from Hebei."

units.zh: 妃曰：「非謀也，我子母亡國之餘，安敢與人爭天下！」
units.en: The lady replied, "That is no plan at all. My son and I are all that remain of a fallen house—how could we dare vie with others for the empire!"
units.literal: The consort said: "That is no plan. My son and I are remnants of a perished state—how dare we contend with others for the realm!"

units.zh: 眾議籍籍，猶以把城為詞。
units.en: Debate raged on, but many still insisted on defending the walls.
units.literal: The crowd's discussion was clamorous, yet still used holding the city as their argument.

units.zh: 審交曰：「余燕人也，今城有燕軍，固合為燕謀，然事機有所不可。
units.en: Shenjiao said, "I am a man of Yan, and with Yan troops in the city one might think we should act for Yan—but the moment will not permit it.
units.literal: Shenjiao said: "I am a man of Yan; now the city has Yan troops and ought indeed to plot for Yan, yet the circumstances of the moment will not allow it.

units.zh: 此城經敵軍破除之後，民力空匱，餘眾幸存，若更謀之不臧，閉門拒守，一月之內，無復遺類。
units.en: The enemy has already gutted this city. The people are spent and only a remnant survives. If we plot badly again, shut the gates, and try to hold out, within a month there will be no one left alive.
units.literal: This city, after the enemy army ravaged it, has its people's strength emptied and depleted; the survivors barely remain. If we plot unwisely again, shut the gates and refuse to yield, within a month none will be left.

units.zh: 諸君勿言，宜從太妃處分。」
units.en: Say no more, gentlemen. Do as the princess mother directs."
units.literal: Gentlemen, speak no more; you should follow the Great Consort's disposition."

units.zh: 繇是從益遣使往太原貢奉。
units.en: On that basis Congyi sent envoys to Taiyuan with tribute and submission.
units.literal: Thereupon Congyi sent envoys to Taiyuan with tribute.

units.zh: 高祖至汴，罷使歸班。
units.en: When Gaozu reached Bian he was relieved of special duty and returned to regular court service.
units.literal: When Gaozu reached Bian, the commission was ended and he returned to the regular roster.

units.zh: 隱帝嗣位，用為汝州防禦使。
units.en: When Emperor Yin succeeded he was appointed defense commissioner of Ruzhou.
units.literal: When Emperor Yin succeeded, he was used as defense commissioner of Ruzhou.

units.zh: 汝為近輔，號為難治，審交盡去煩弊，無擾於民，百姓歌之。
units.en: Ruzhou lay close to the capital and had a reputation for being hard to govern, but Shenjiao swept away abuses, left the people unmolested, and the folk sang his praise.
units.literal: Ru was a nearby auxiliary district, reputed hard to govern; Shenjiao completely removed vexations and abuses, did not disturb the people, and the common folk sang of him.

units.zh: 乾祐二年春，卒，年七十四。
units.en: He died in the spring of Qianyou 2, at the age of seventy-four.
units.literal: In spring of the second year of Qianyou he died, aged seventy-four.

units.zh: 郡人聚哭柩前所，列狀乞留葬本州界，立碑起祠，以時致祭。
units.en: The people of the prefecture gathered to weep before his coffin and petitioned that he be buried within their borders, with a stele and shrine and regular sacrifices.
units.literal: The people of the commandery gathered to weep before the bier, submitted a petition asking that he be buried within the boundaries of the prefecture, and requested a stele and shrine with seasonal offerings.

units.zh: 本州以聞，詔曰：「朝廷之制，皆有舊章，牧守之官，比無贈典。
units.en: The prefecture reported this to the throne. An edict declared, "The court has long had fixed statutes, and regional governors as a rule receive no special posthumous honors.
units.literal: The prefecture reported upward; an edict said: "The court's institutions all have old statutes; prefects and governors as a rule have no posthumous rites.

units.zh: 其或政能殊異，惠及蒸黎，生有令名，沒留遺愛，褒賢獎善，豈限彜章。
units.en: Yet when an official's conduct is truly exceptional, his kindness reaches the people, he wins a fine name in life and leaves devotion behind in death, to honor the worthy and reward goodness should not be bound by ordinary rule.
units.literal: Yet if administrative ability is exceptionally outstanding, benefit reaches the common folk, in life there is a fine name and in death lingering affection remains, to praise the worthy and reward the good—how should one be confined by ordinary statutes?

units.zh: 可特贈太尉，吏民所請宜依。」
units.en: Let him be specially posthumously appointed Grand Commandant, and grant what the officials and people have asked."
units.literal: He may specially be posthumously made Grand Commandant; what the officials and people request should be granted."

units.zh: 故相國、太師、秦國公馮道聞之曰：「予嘗為劉汝州僚佐，知其為人廉平慈善，無害之良吏也。
units.en: When Feng Dao, former chief minister, Grand Preceptor, and Duke of Qin, heard this he said, "I once served under Liu of Ruzhou and know him to have been an honest, fair, and kindly official who harmed no one—a true good magistrate.
units.literal: The former Chancellor, Grand Preceptor, and Duke of Qin Feng Dao heard and said: "I once served as Liu of Ruzhou's subordinate and know him to be honest, fair, charitable—a good official who harms none.

units.zh: 刺遼、磁，治陳、襄、青，皆稱平允，不顯殊尤，其理汝也，又安有異哉！
units.en: As prefect of Liao and Ci and as administrator of Chen, Xiang, and Qing he was always called fair and steady, never marked by any extraordinary feat. His rule in Ru was no different!
units.literal: As prefect of Liao and Ci, governing Chen, Xiang, and Qing—all were called fair and even, without showing special excellence; his governing Ru—how could there have been any difference!

units.zh: 民之租賦不能減也，徭役不能息也，寒者不能衣也，餒者不能食也，百姓自汲汲然，而使君何有於我哉！
units.en: He could not cut their taxes or end their labor service, clothe the cold or feed the hungry. The people were busy with their own struggles—what had their magistrate really done for them!
units.literal: The people's rent and tax could not be reduced, corvée labor could not be stilled, the cold could not be clothed, the hungry could not be fed; the common folk were naturally in distress—what did the magistrate have to do with us!

units.zh: 然身死之日，致黎民懷感如此者，誠以不行鞭樸，不行刻剝，不因公而循私，不害物以利己，確然行良吏之事，薄罰宥過，謹身節用，安俸祿、守禮分而已。
units.en: Yet on the day he died the people were moved to such grief precisely because he used no lash or rod, exacted nothing harshly, never bent public office to private ends or harmed others for his own gain. He simply did what a good official should: light penalties, pardon of small faults, restraint and thrift, contentment with his salary, and observance of his proper place.
units.literal: Yet on the day of his death to move the common people to such gratitude was truly because he did not use the whip, did not practice harsh exaction, did not use public office for private ends, did not harm things to benefit himself—steadfastly performing a good official's duties, light punishment and pardoning faults, keeping the body restrained and frugal in use, content with salary and observing ritual bounds, that is all.

units.zh: 凡從事於斯者，孰不能乎！
units.en: Who among those in office could not have done as much!
units.literal: All who engage in this—who cannot do it!

units.zh: 但前之守土者不能如是，是以汝民咨嗟愛慕。
units.en: Only because earlier governors had failed to do even that much did the people of Ru sigh and cherish him as they did.
units.literal: Only the previous holders of the soil could not be like this; therefore the people of Ru sighed and loved and admired him.

units.zh: 今天下戎馬之後，四方兇盜之餘，杼柚空而賦斂繁，人民稀而倉稟匱，謂之康泰，未易輕言。
units.en: Today, after armies have trampled the empire and bandits have ravaged every quarter, the looms stand idle while taxes remain heavy, the population is thin while the granaries are bare—to speak of peace and plenty is no easy thing.
units.literal: Now after war-horses throughout the realm, after violent bandits in the four quarters, looms are empty yet levies are heavy, the people are sparse yet granaries are depleted—to call it peace and prosperity is not lightly said.

units.zh: 侯伯牧宰，若能哀矜之，不至聚斂，不殺無辜之民，民為邦本，政為民本，和平寬易，即劉君之政安足稱耶！
units.en: If every lord and prefect could show compassion, refrain from crushing levies, and spare innocent lives—if the people are the root of the state and government the root of the people—then peace, leniency, and ease alone would scarcely make Liu's rule worth special praise!
units.literal: If marquises, earls, shepherds, and magistrates could show compassion, not reach to mass exaction, not kill innocent people—people are the state's root, government is the people's root—peace, leniency, and ease: then even Lord Liu's administration—how is it enough to be praised!

units.zh: 復河患不至於令名哉！」
units.en: And who that merely avoided harming the people would fail to win a fine name!"
units.literal: Again, what worry is there of not attaining a fine reputation!"

units.zh: 道仍為著哀詞六章，鐫於墓碑之陰焉。
units.en: Feng Dao also composed six stanzas of lament and had them engraved on the back of the tomb stele.
units.literal: Dao still composed six chapters of lament and had them carved on the reverse of the tomb stele.

units.zh: 武漢球，澤州人也。
units.en: Wu Hanqiu was a native of Zezhou.
units.literal: Wu Hanqiu was a man of Zezhou.

units.zh: 少拳勇，潞帥李嗣昭倚為親信，事唐莊宗、明宗，繼為禁軍裨校。
units.en: As a youth he was famed for courage in combat. Li Sizhao, military governor of Lu, trusted him as a confidant. He served under Zhuangzong and Mingzong of Tang and rose to staff officer in the palace guards.
units.literal: In youth he was bold in boxing; the Lu commander Li Sizhao relied on him as a trusted intimate. He served Tang Emperors Zhuangzong and Mingzong and successively became a staff officer of the palace guard.

units.zh: 清泰中，會晉高祖引契丹為援，與朝廷隔絕，遂歸晉祖。
units.en: During the Qingtai era, when Jin Gaozu called in the Khitan and was cut off from the Tang court, Hanqiu went over to him.
units.literal: In Qingtai, when Jin Gaozu brought the Khitan as aid and was cut off from the court, he then submitted to Jin's founder.

units.zh: 天福初，授趙州刺史，入為奉國軍都指揮使，出刺曹州。
units.en: Early in Tianfu he became prefect of Zhaozhou, then commander of the Fengguo Army, and later governor of Caozhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu he was appointed prefect of Zhaozhou, entered as commander of the Fengguo Army, and went out to govern Caozhou.

units.zh: 開運初，遷耀州團練使。
units.en: At the start of the Kaiyun era he was made regimentation commissioner of Yaozhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun he was transferred to regimentation commissioner of Yaozhou.

units.zh: 高祖至東京，授洺州刺史，漢球以目疾年高辭郡，帝曰：「廣平小郡，卿臥理有餘，無以疾辭。」
units.en: When Gaozu reached the Eastern Capital he appointed Hanqiu prefect of Mingzhou. Hanqiu pleaded eye trouble and old age, but the emperor said, "Guangping is a small prefecture. You can govern it from your bed with ease—do not refuse because of illness."
units.literal: When Gaozu reached the Eastern Capital he was appointed prefect of Mingzhou; Hanqiu, citing eye ailment and advanced age, declined the prefecture. The emperor said: "Guangping is a small commandery; you, governing from your couch, have more than enough capacity—do not decline on account of illness."

units.zh: 至郡未期，復以目疾請代而免。
units.en: Before his term was out he again asked to be replaced because of his eyes and was excused.
units.literal: When he reached the commandery, before his term was complete, he again requested replacement because of eye ailment and was relieved.

units.zh: 乾祐二年秋，卒於京師。
units.en: In the autumn of Qianyou 2 he died in the capital.
units.literal: In autumn of the second year of Qianyou he died in the capital.

units.zh: 漢球雖出自行伍，然長於撫理，常以掊斂為戒，民懷其惠，身死之日，家無餘財。
units.en: Though he rose from the ranks, Hanqiu excelled at humane administration and always shunned extortion. The people cherished him, and when he died his family had nothing left.
units.literal: Although Hanqiu came from the ranks, he was skilled at soothing governance and constantly took exaction as a warning; the people cherished his kindness, and on the day of his death his household had no surplus wealth.

units.zh: 有管回者，漢球守郡日，辟為判官。
units.en: A man named Guan Hui had served as his chief aide when Hanqiu held the prefecture.
units.literal: There was one Guan Hui whom, on the days when Hanqiu held the commandery, he recruited as chief aide.

units.zh: 及漢球卒於汴，回在洺州未之知，一日，忽謂所親曰：「太保遣人召我。」
units.en: When Hanqiu died at Bian, Hui was still in Mingzhou and knew nothing of it. One day he suddenly told his intimates, "The Grand Guardian has sent for me."
units.literal: When Hanqiu died at Bian, Hui was at Mingzhou and did not know it. One day he suddenly said to those close to him: "The Grand Guardian has sent men to summon me."

units.zh: 遂沐浴，新衣冠，無疾瞑目而終。
units.en: He bathed, dressed in fresh robes, and died peacefully without illness.
units.literal: He then bathed, put on fresh cap and robes, and without illness closed his eyes and died.

units.zh: 家人不知其故，後數日，方聞漢球卒。
units.en: His family did not understand why until, days later, word came that Hanqiu was dead.
units.literal: His family did not know the reason; several days later they finally heard that Hanqiu had died.

units.zh: 張瓘，同州車渡村人，故太原監軍使承業之猶子也。
units.en: Zhang Guan came from Chedu Village in Tongzhou and was a nephew of the former Taiyuan military overseer Zhang Chengye.
units.literal: Zhang Guan was a man of Chedu Village in Tongzhou, a nephew of the former Taiyuan military overseer Zhang Chengye.

units.zh: 承業，《唐書》有傳。
units.en: Chengye has a biography in the Tang History.
units.literal: Chengye has a biography in the Book of Tang.

units.zh: 唐天祐中，承業佐唐武皇、莊宗有功，甚見委遇，瓘聞之，與昆仲五人，自故裏奔於太原，莊宗皆任用之。
units.en: During Tang Tianyou Chengye served the Martial Emperor and Zhuangzong with distinction and won great trust. When Guan heard of his success, he and his brothers—five in all—left their village for Taiyuan, and Zhuangzong gave them all posts.
units.literal: In Tang Tianyou, Chengye aided Tang's Martial Emperor and Zhuangzong with merit and was greatly entrusted and favored. Guan heard of this; with five brothers he fled from their old home to Taiyuan, and Zhuangzong employed them all.

units.zh: 瓘天祐十三年補麟州刺史。
units.en: In Tianyou 13 Guan was appointed prefect of Linzhou.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianyou Guan was appointed to fill the post of prefect of Linzhou.

units.zh: 承業治家嚴毅，小過無所容恕，一侄為磁州副使，以其殺河西賣羊客，承業立捕斬之。
units.en: Chengye ran his household with stern discipline and tolerated no small fault. One nephew served as deputy commissioner of Cizhou; when he killed a sheep merchant from Hexi, Chengye had him seized and executed at once.
units.literal: Chengye governed the family with stern severity; small faults found no forgiveness. One nephew was deputy commissioner of Cizhou; because he killed a sheep merchant from Hexi, Chengye immediately had him seized and beheaded.

units.zh: 常誡瓘等曰：「汝車渡村百姓劉開道下賊，慣作非為，今須改行，若故態不除，死無日矣。」
units.en: He often warned Guan and his brothers, "You villagers of Chedu followed the bandit Liu Kaidao and grew used to wrongdoing. Reform yourselves now—if you do not, your deaths will come soon."
units.literal: He often admonished Guan and the others: "You Chedu Village folk followed the bandit Liu Kaidao, accustomed to wrongdoing; now you must reform your conduct—if the old ways are not removed, the day of death is not far."

units.zh: 故瓘所至不敢誅求。
units.en: For that reason Guan never dared to squeeze the people wherever he served.
units.literal: Therefore wherever Guan went he did not dare to extort.

units.zh: 晉天福中，為密州刺史，秩滿入居環衛。
units.en: Under Jin Tianfu he governed Mizhou, and when his term ended he entered palace-guard service at court.
units.literal: In Jin Tianfu he was prefect of Mizhou; when his term was complete he entered to dwell in the palace guard.

units.zh: 乾祐三年夏，卒於官，輟視朝一日。
units.en: In the summer of Qianyou 3 he died in office, and the court suspended audiences for a day.
units.literal: In summer of the third year of Qianyou he died in office; court audiences were suspended for one day.

units.zh: 李殷，薊州人也。
units.en: Li Yin was a native of Jizhou.
units.literal: Li Yin was a man of Jizhou.

units.zh: 自後唐莊宗、明宗、晉高祖朝，以偏校遞遷，歷官至檢校司徒，累為郡守。
units.en: From the reigns of Zhuangzong and Mingzong of Later Tang through Jin Gaozu he rose step by step from junior officer to honorary Minister of Works and held one prefectural post after another.
units.literal: From the courts of Later Tang's Zhuangzong and Mingzong and Jin's Gaozu, as a junior officer he was transferred in succession, rose in office to honorary Minister of Works, and repeatedly held prefectural governorships.

units.zh: 性沈厚，所蒞無苛暴之名。
units.en: He was sober and steady by nature and never earned a reputation for harsh rule.
units.literal: His nature was deep and steady; wherever he arrived there was no name for harsh cruelty.

units.zh: 晉少帝御契丹於澶淵，殷典禁旅，駕還，授鄜州留後，俄加檢校太保。
units.en: When Emperor Shao of Jin faced the Khitan at Chanyuan, Yin commanded the palace guard. After the emperor's return he was made regent of Fuzhou and soon after honorary Grand Guardian.
units.literal: When Jin's Emperor Shao faced the Khitan at Chanyuan, Yin commanded the palace guard; when the carriage returned he was appointed regent of Fuzhou, and soon after given honorary Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 開運中，授定州節度使，將行，啟少帝曰：「臣之此行，破敵必矣。」
units.en: During Kaiyun he was appointed military commissioner of Dingzhou. Before leaving he told Emperor Shao, "On this campaign I shall surely crush the enemy."
units.literal: In Kaiyun he was appointed military commissioner of Dingzhou; about to depart, he reported to Emperor Shao: "On this journey of mine, defeating the enemy is certain."

units.zh: 眾皆壯其言，及至郡，威略無聞，敵再至，首納降款。
units.en: Everyone cheered his bold words, but once he reached his post no sign of military prowess appeared. When the enemy returned he was the first to offer surrender.
units.literal: All were impressed by his words; when he reached the commandery, no fame for martial strategy was heard; the enemy came again and he was first to submit a surrender document.

units.zh: 後隨契丹至常山，其將解裏遣殷與契丹首領楊安，同拒我師於洺水，俄而安退，殷以橐裝駝馬遺安。
units.en: He later followed the Khitan to Changshan. The Khitan general Jieli sent Yin with the Khitan leader Yang An to block our army at the Ming River. When Yang An soon withdrew, Yin gave him pack camels loaded with goods.
units.literal: Later he followed the Khitan to Changshan; their general Jieli sent Yin together with the Khitan leader Yang An to jointly resist our army at the Ming River. Soon An withdrew; Yin gave An pack animals and camels loaded with goods.

units.zh: 安既北走，殷匿於丘墓獲免，馳以歸我。
units.en: After Yang An fled north, Yin hid among tombs and mounds until he could escape, then rode back to our side.
units.literal: When An had already fled north, Yin hid among tombs and mounds and escaped; he galloped to return to us.

units.zh: 高祖嘉其首赴朝闕，及魏州平，以甘陵乏帥，乃命殷為貝州節度使，加檢校太傅。
units.en: Gaozu praised him for being the first to return to court. When Weizhou was pacified and Ganling lacked a commander, he appointed Yin military commissioner of Beizhou with the additional title of honorary Grand Tutor.
units.literal: Gaozu praised him for being first to hurry to the court; when Weizhou was pacified, because Ganling lacked a commander he ordered Yin as military commissioner of Beizhou and added honorary Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 乾祐初，卒於鎮。
units.en: Early in Qianyou he died in office.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou he died at his post.

units.zh: 詔贈太師。
units.en: The court posthumously appointed him Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: An edict posthumously made him Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 劉在明，幽州人。
units.en: Liu Zaiming was a native of Youzhou.
units.literal: Liu Zaiming was a man of Youzhou.

units.zh: 少有膽氣，本州節度使劉守光用為親信，出為平塞軍使。
units.en: As a youth he was bold and spirited. Liu Shouguang, military governor of the region, took him as a confidant and later sent him out as commander of the Pingsai garrison.
units.literal: In youth he had courage and spirit; the prefectural military commissioner Liu Shouguang used him as a trusted intimate and sent him out as commissioner of Pingsai Army.

units.zh: 守光敗，歸於太原，唐莊宗收為列校。
units.en: When Shouguang fell he made his way to Taiyuan, where Zhuangzong of Tang enrolled him among the officer corps.
units.literal: When Shouguang was defeated, he returned to Taiyuan; Tang's Zhuangzong took him in as a ranked officer.

units.zh: 明宗時，為捧聖左廂都指揮使，領和州刺史。
units.en: Under Mingzong he commanded the left wing of the Pengsheng Guard while also holding the prefecture of Hezhou.
units.literal: In Mingzong's time he was commander of the left wing of the Pengsheng Guard and concurrently held the prefecture of Hezhou.

units.zh: 從幸汴州，至滎陽，聞朱守殷叛，用為前鋒。
units.en: He accompanied the emperor to Bianzhou and, when they reached Xingyang and heard that Zhu Shouyin had rebelled, was placed in the vanguard.
units.literal: Following the imperial progress to Bianzhou, when they reached Xingyang they heard Zhu Shouyin had rebelled and he was used as vanguard.

units.zh: 至汴城，率先登城，賊平，授汴州馬步軍都指揮使。
units.en: At Bian he was the first to scale the walls. After the rebels were crushed he was made commander of all horse and foot forces at Bianzhou.
units.literal: When he reached Bian city he was first to ascend the wall; when the rebels were pacified he was appointed commander of Bianzhou's horse and foot armies.

units.zh: 應順初，為貝州刺史。
units.en: Early in the Yingshun era he became prefect of Beizhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yingshun he was prefect of Beizhou.

units.zh: 明年，移趙州，兼北面行營馬軍都指揮使，以軍戍易州。
units.en: The following year he was moved to Zhaozhou as northern campaign cavalry commander and stationed his troops at Yizhou.
units.literal: The next year he was transferred to Zhaozhou, concurrently northern campaign army cavalry commander, and garrisoned Yizhou with troops.

units.zh: 清泰末，幽州節度使趙德鈞引軍赴團柏谷，路由易州，取在明軍從。
units.en: Late in Qingtai, Zhao Dejun of Youzhou marched toward Tuanbai Valley by way of Yizhou and took Zaiming's force with him.
units.literal: Late in Qingtai, Youzhou military commissioner Zhao Dejun led troops to Tuanbai Valley; the route passed through Yizhou, and he took Zaiming's army to follow.

units.zh: 及德鈞兵敗，在明奔歸懷州，唐末帝令與萇從簡同守河陽。
units.en: When Dejun was defeated, Zaiming fled to Huaizhou. The last Tang emperor ordered him and Chang Congjian to hold Heyang together.
units.literal: When Dejun's army was defeated, Zaiming fled back to Huaizhou; Tang's final emperor ordered him to defend Heyang together with Chang Congjian.

units.zh: 晉祖至，乃迎之，京都事定，出為單州刺史。
units.en: When the Jin founder arrived he went out to welcome him. After the capital was secured he was appointed prefect of Shanzhou.
units.literal: When Jin's founder arrived, he then welcomed him; when the capital affairs were settled he went out as prefect of Shanzhou.

units.zh: 天福中，李金全以安州叛，在明從李守貞攻之，大破淮賊，以功授安州防禦使，明年，移絳州。
units.en: During Tianfu, Li Jinquan rebelled from Anzhou. Zaiming joined Li Shouzhen in the attack, routed the Huai rebels, and was made defense commissioner of Anzhou for his service. The next year he was transferred to Jiangzhou.
units.literal: In Tianfu, Li Jinquan rebelled with Anzhou; Zaiming followed Li Shouzhen to attack him, greatly defeated the Huai bandits, and for merit was appointed defense commissioner of Anzhou; the next year he was transferred to Jiangzhou.

units.zh: 楊光遠據青州叛，召為行營馬步軍都指揮使，領齊州防禦使。
units.en: When Yang Guangyuan rebelled from Qingzhou he was summoned as campaign commander of all horse and foot forces and concurrently made defense commissioner of Qizhou.
units.literal: Yang Guangyuan held Qingzhou and rebelled; he was summoned as campaign horse-and-foot commander and concurrently held defense commissioner of Qizhou.

units.zh: 青州平，遷相州留後，歷邢州、晉州留後。
units.en: After Qingzhou was pacified he became regent of Xiangzhou and later served as regent at Xingzhou and Jinzhou in turn.
units.literal: When Qingzhou was pacified he was transferred to regent of Xiangzhou and successively held regencies at Xingzhou and Jinzhou.

units.zh: 〈（《通鑒》：契丹犯闕，建雄留後劉在明朝於契丹，以節度副使駱知朗知州事。）〉
units.en: (《Zizhi Tongjian》: When the Khitan invaded the capital, Liu Zaiming, regent of Jianxiong, had an audience with them and put Deputy Commissioner Luo Zhilang in charge of the prefecture.)〉
units.literal: (《Zizhi Tongjian》: When the Khitan violated the capital, Jianxiong regent Liu Zaiming had an audience with the Khitan and made deputy commissioner Luo Zhilang administer the prefectural affairs.)〉

units.zh: 高祖踐阼，授幽州道行營都部署。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne he was made overall commander of the Youzhou circuit campaign.
units.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne he was appointed overall deployer of the Youzhou circuit campaign.

units.zh: 時契丹守中山，在明出師經略，契丹乃棄城而去，遂授鎮州留後。
units.en: The Khitan then held Zhongshan. Zaiming marched against them and drove them from the city, and he was appointed regent of Zhenzhou.
units.literal: At the time the Khitan held Zhongshan; Zaiming led troops in planning and strategy, and the Khitan then abandoned the city and left; he was then appointed regent of Zhenzhou.

units.zh: 乾祐元年五月，正授鎮州節度使。
units.en: In the fifth month of Qianyou 1 he was formally appointed military commissioner of Zhenzhou.
units.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Qianyou he was formally appointed military commissioner of Zhenzhou.

units.zh: 六月，以疾卒於鎮。
units.en: In the sixth month he died of illness in office.
units.literal: In the sixth month he died of illness at his post.

units.zh: 贈侍中。
units.en: He was posthumously appointed Palace Attendant.
units.literal: He was posthumously made Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 馬萬，澶州人也。
units.en: Ma Wan was a native of Chanzhou.
units.literal: Ma Wan was a man of Chanzhou.

units.zh: 少從軍，善水遊。
units.en: He entered the army young and was an expert swimmer.
units.literal: In youth he followed the army and was skilled at swimming.

units.zh: 唐莊宗與梁軍對壘於河上，莊宗於德勝渡夾河立南北寨。
units.en: When Zhuangzong of Tang faced the Liang army on the Yellow River, he built north and south camps on either bank at Desheng Ford.
units.literal: Tang's Zhuangzong and the Liang army faced each other on the river; Zhuangzong at Desheng Ford established north and south stockades on both banks.

units.zh: 會梁軍急攻南寨，於中流聯戰艦以絕援路，晝夜攻城者三日，寨將氏延賞告急於莊宗。
units.en: The Liang forces then pressed hard against the southern camp, chaining warships across the river to block reinforcements and attacking day and night for three days. The camp commander Shi Yanshang sent urgent word to Zhuangzong.
units.literal: It happened that the Liang army urgently attacked the south stockade, linking warships midstream to cut off the relief route; they assaulted the city day and night for three days, and the stockade commander Shi Yanshang reported emergency to Zhuangzong.

units.zh: 莊宗隔河望敵，無如之何，乃召人能水遊破賊者。
units.en: Zhuangzong watched the enemy from the far bank, helpless, and called for men who could swim across and break the siege.
units.literal: Zhuangzong gazed at the enemy across the river with nothing to be done about it, and then summoned men who could swim and break the enemy.

units.zh: 時萬兄弟皆應募，遂潛行入南寨，往來者三，又助燒船艦，汴軍遂退。
units.en: Wan and his brothers volunteered, slipped into the southern camp three times, and helped set the enemy ships afire. The Bian army then withdrew.
units.literal: At the time Wan and his brothers all answered the call; they then secretly entered the south stockade, going back and forth three times, and also helped burn the ships, and the Bian army then withdrew.

units.zh: 由此升為水軍小校，漸典禁軍，遙領刺史，累遷奉國左廂都指揮使、泗州防禦使。
units.en: For this he was promoted in the navy, then rose through the palace guards, held a prefecture in absentia, and eventually became commander of the left wing of the Fengguo Army and defense commissioner of Sizhou.
units.literal: From this he was promoted to junior officer of the naval forces, gradually commanded the palace guard, held the prefecture of Sizhou in absentia, and was repeatedly transferred to commander of the left wing of the Fengguo Army and defense commissioner of Sizhou.

units.zh: 晉天福二年夏，範延光叛於鄴，牙將孫銳率兵至黎陽，朝廷遣侍衛馬軍都指揮使白奉進領兵渡滑州，萬亦預其行。
units.en: In the summer of Jin Tianfu 2, Fan Yanguang rebelled at Ye. Sun Rui marched on Liyang, and the court sent Bai Fengjin with the palace cavalry through Huazhou. Wan went with them.
units.literal: In summer of the second year of Jin Tianfu, Fan Yanguang rebelled at Ye; staff general Sun Rui led troops to Liyang; the court sent palace guard cavalry commander Bai Fengjin to lead troops across Huazhou, and Wan also took part in the expedition.

units.zh: 時滑州節度使符彥饒潛通鄴下，殺白奉進於牙署。
units.en: The military commissioner of Huazhou, Fu Yanrao, was secretly in league with Ye and murdered Bai Fengjin at headquarters.
units.literal: At the time Huazhou military commissioner Fu Yanrao secretly communicated with Ye and killed Bai Fengjin in the headquarters.

units.zh: 萬領本軍兵士將助亂，會奉國右廂都指揮使盧順密亦以兵至，諭以逆順，萬不得已，與順密急趨公府，執彥饒生送闕下。
units.en: Wan was about to join the mutiny with his men when Lu Shunmi, commander of the Fengguo right wing, arrived and persuaded him of right and wrong. Wan then rushed with Shunmi to the government hall, seized Yanrao alive, and sent him to the capital.
units.literal: Wan led his own army's soldiers intending to aid the disorder; it happened that Fengguo right-wing commander Lu Shunmi also arrived with troops, explained loyalty and rebellion, and Wan had no choice but to hurry with Shunmi to the government office, seize Yanrao alive, and send him to the capital.

units.zh: 朝廷即以萬為滑州節度使，而盧順密酬之甚淺。
units.en: The court at once made Wan military commissioner of Huazhou, but rewarded Lu Shunmi only meagerly.
units.literal: The court immediately made Wan military commissioner of Huazhou, while Lu Shunmi's reward for him was very slight.

units.zh: 居無何，晉高祖稍知其事，即以順密為涇州兵馬留後，漸薄於萬。
units.en: Before long Gaozu learned what had really happened. He made Shunmi regent at Jingzhou and gradually came to favor Wan less.
units.literal: Before long, Jin Gaozu gradually learned of the affair and immediately made Shunmi regent of Jingzhou's troops and horses, gradually treating Wan with less favor.

units.zh: 萬鎮鄧州，未幾罷鎮，授上將軍，以目疾致仕。
units.en: Wan governed Dengzhou, but was soon removed and made Senior General before retiring because of eye trouble.
units.literal: Wan garrisoned Dengzhou; before long his garrison was ended; he was given Senior General and retired because of eye disease.

units.zh: 乾祐三年四月卒。
units.en: He died in the fourth month of Qianyou 3.
units.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Qianyou he died.

units.zh: 輟視朝一日。
units.en: The court suspended audiences for a day.
units.literal: Court audiences were suspended for one day.

units.zh: 李彥從，字士元，汾州孝義人。
units.en: Li Yancong, courtesy name Shiyuan, was a native of Xiaoyi in Fenzhou.
units.literal: Li Yancong, style name Shiyuan, was a man of Xiaoyi in Fenzhou.

units.zh: 父德，麟州司馬。
units.en: His father De had been assistant prefect of Linzhou.
units.literal: His father De was assistant prefect of Linzhou.

units.zh: 彥從少習武藝，出行伍間，高祖典禁軍，以鄉里之舊，任為親信。
units.en: Yancong trained in the martial arts from youth and rose through the ranks. When Gaozu commanded the palace guard he took Yancong into his confidence as a fellow townsman.
units.literal: Yancong in youth studied martial arts and moved among the ranks; when Gaozu commanded the palace guard, because of their old ties from the same district he was employed as a trusted intimate.

units.zh: 國初，用為左飛龍使、檢校司空。
units.en: At the founding of the dynasty he was made Left Flying Dragon Commissioner and honorary Minister of Works.
units.literal: At the founding of the state he was used as Left Flying Dragon Commissioner and honorary Minister of Works.

units.zh: 鎮州逐敵之際，請兵於朝廷，高祖令彥從率軍赴之。
units.en: When Zhenzhou needed troops to drive off the enemy, Gaozu ordered Yancong to lead a force there.
units.literal: At the time when Zhenzhou was driving off the enemy, troops were requested from the court, and Gaozu ordered Yancong to lead an army to go there.

units.zh: 乾祐初，領恩州刺史。
units.en: Early in Qianyou he held the prefecture of Enzhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou he held the prefecture of Enzhou.

units.zh: 趙暉討王景崇於岐下，彥從為兵馬都監，破川軍有功，賊平，授濮州刺史，治有政能，百姓悅之。
units.en: When Zhao Hui campaigned against Wang Jingchong at Qi, Yancong served as cavalry inspector, distinguished himself against the Chuan forces, and after the rebels were crushed was made prefect of Puzhou. He governed capably and won the people's approval.
units.literal: Zhao Hui attacked Wang Jingchong below Qi; Yancong was overall cavalry inspector, broke the Chuan army with merit; when the bandits were pacified he was appointed prefect of Puzhou, governed with administrative ability, and the people were pleased.

units.zh: 乾祐三年冬，卒於郡。
units.en: He died in office in the winter of Qianyou 3.
units.literal: In winter of the third year of Qianyou he died in the commandery.

units.zh: 郭謹，字守節，太原晉陽人。
units.en: Guo Jin, courtesy name Shoujie, was a native of Jinyang in Taiyuan.
units.literal: Guo Jin, style name Shoujie, was a man of Jinyang in Taiyuan.

units.zh: 謹少從軍，能騎射，歷河中教練使。
units.en: He entered the army young, was skilled at horsemanship and archery, and served as training commissioner at Hezhong.
units.literal: Jin in youth followed the army, could ride and shoot, and served as training commissioner in Hezhong.

units.zh: 晉天福中，遷奉國右廂都指揮使，領禺州刺史。
units.en: During Jin Tianfu he became commander of the Fengguo Guard's right wing and prefect of Yuzhou.
units.literal: In Tianfu of Jin he was transferred to commander of the right wing of the Fengguo Guard and held the prefecture of Yuzhou.

units.zh: 三年，轉奉國左廂都指揮、泗州防禦使。
units.en: In year 3 he moved to commander of the Fengguo left wing and defense commissioner of Sizhou.
units.literal: In the third year he was transferred to commander of the left wing of Fengguo and defense commissioner of Sizhou.

units.zh: 歲餘，授侍衛步軍都指揮使兼寧江軍節度使。
units.en: A little over a year later he was made overall commander of the palace infantry and military commissioner of Ningjiang.
units.literal: After more than a year he was appointed overall commander of the palace guard infantry and military commissioner of Ningjiang.

units.zh: 六年，從幸鄴。
units.en: In year 6 he accompanied the emperor to Ye.
units.literal: In the sixth year he accompanied the emperor to Ye.

units.zh: 七年，晉祖崩，少帝即位，授彰德軍節度使，領軍如故。
units.en: In year 7, after the Jin emperor's death and the Young Emperor's accession, he was made military commissioner of Zhangde while keeping his command.
units.literal: In the seventh year the Jin ancestor died and the Young Emperor succeeded; he was appointed military commissioner of Zhangde, retaining his military post as before.

units.zh: 開運初，出授鄜州。
units.en: Early in Kaiyun he was posted to Fuzhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun he was sent out to hold Fuzhou.

units.zh: 二年，入為左神武統軍。
units.en: In year 2 he became overall commander of the Left Divine Martial Army.
units.literal: In the second year he entered the capital as overall commander of the Left Divine Martial Army.

units.zh: 三年，復鎮鄜州。
units.en: In year 3 he returned to govern Fuzhou.
units.literal: In the third year he again garrisoned Fuzhou.

units.zh: 高祖踐阼，以鄉國舊臣，加檢校太尉，移鎮滑臺。
units.en: When Gaozu took the throne he was made honorary Grand Marshal as a veteran from their homeland and transferred to Huatai.
units.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne, because he was an old follower from the homeland he was given honorary Grand Marshal and transferred to garrison Huatai.

units.zh: 乾祐初，復授彰德軍節度使。
units.en: Early in Qianyou he was again made military commissioner of Zhangde.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou he was again appointed military commissioner of Zhangde.

units.zh: 二年，就加檢校太師。
units.en: In year 2 he received the further title of honorary Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: In the second year he was further given honorary Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 三年，入朝，加食邑。
units.en: In year 3 he went to court and was granted an enlarged fief.
units.literal: In the third year he came to court and received an increase in his fief.

units.zh: 是歲冬十月，卒於位，年六十。
units.en: He died in office that winter, in the tenth month, at the age of sixty.
units.literal: That winter in the tenth month he died in office, aged sixty.

units.zh: 輟視朝二日，贈侍中。
units.en: Court audiences were suspended for two days, and he was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
units.literal: Court audiences were suspended for two days, and he was posthumously given Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 皇甫立，代北人也。
units.en: Huangfu Li was from northern Dai.
units.literal: Huangfu Li was a man of northern Dai.

units.zh: 唐明宗之刺代州，署為牙校，從歷藩鎮。
units.en: When Emperor Mingzong of Tang governed Daizhou he appointed Li a yamen officer, and Li followed him through successive postings.
units.literal: When Mingzong of Tang was prefect of Daizhou, he appointed Li as a yamen officer; Li followed him through successive provincial commands.

units.zh: 性純謹，明宗深委信之，王建立、安重誨策名委質、皆在立後。
units.en: He was upright and conscientious, and Mingzong trusted him deeply. Wang Jianli and An Chonghui both entered service only after Li had.
units.literal: His nature was pure and dutiful; Mingzong deeply entrusted him. Wang Jianli and An Chonghui both entered service after Li had done so.

units.zh: 明宗踐阼，以立為忻州刺史。
units.en: When Mingzong took the throne he made Li prefect of Xinzhou.
units.literal: When Mingzong ascended the throne he made Li prefect of Xinzhou.

units.zh: 長興末，轉洺州團練使。
units.en: Late in Changxing he became regimental commissioner of Mingzhou.
units.literal: At the end of Changxing he was transferred to regimental commissioner of Mingzhou.

units.zh: 應順初，遷鄜州節度使，檢校太保。
units.en: Early in Yingshun he was made military commissioner of Fuzhou and honorary Grand Guardian.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yingshun he was transferred to military commissioner of Fuzhou and honorary Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 清泰三年春，移鎮潞州，未幾，改華州。
units.en: In the spring of Qingtai 3 he was transferred to Luzhou, and soon after to Huazhou.
units.literal: In spring of the third year of Qingtai he was transferred to garrison Luzhou; before long he was changed to Huazhou.

units.zh: 晉天福中，授左神武統軍。
units.en: During Jin Tianfu he was made overall commander of the Left Divine Martial Army.
units.literal: In Tianfu of Jin he was appointed overall commander of the Left Divine Martial Army.

units.zh: 少帝即位，歷左金吾衛上將軍，累官至檢校太尉。
units.en: After the Young Emperor's accession he served as Senior General of the Left Golden Crow Guard and eventually reached honorary Grand Marshal.
units.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded he served as Senior General of the Left Golden Crow Guard and rose through offices to honorary Grand Marshal.

units.zh: 高祖定天下，授特進、太子太師致仕。
units.en: After Gaozu secured the realm he was granted Special Advancement and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and allowed to retire.
units.literal: When Gaozu settled the realm he was given Special Advancement and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired.

units.zh: 乾祐二年秋卒。
units.en: He died in the autumn of Qianyou 2.
units.literal: In autumn of the second year of Qianyou he died.

units.zh: 白再榮，本蕃部人也。
units.en: Bai Zairong was originally from the frontier tribes.
units.literal: Bai Zairong was originally a man of the barbarian tribes.

units.zh: 少從軍，累遷護聖左廂指揮使。
units.en: He entered the army young and eventually became commander of the left wing of the Husheng Guard.
units.literal: In youth he followed the army and was repeatedly transferred to commander of the left wing of the Husheng Guard.

units.zh: 晉末，契丹入汴，明年，契丹主北去，再榮從部帳至真定。
units.en: Late in Jin the Khitan entered Bian. The next year, as the Khitan emperor withdrew north, Zairong followed the camp to Zhending.
units.literal: At the end of Jin the Khitan entered Bian; the next year the Khitan ruler went north, and Zairong followed the tribal encampment to Zhending.

units.zh: 其年閏七月晦，李筠、何福晉相率殺北帥滿達勒，據甲仗庫，敵勢未退，筠等使人召再榮。
units.en: On the last day of the intercalary seventh month that year, Li Jun and He Fujin led the killing of the Khitan commander Mandale and seized the armory. The enemy had not yet withdrawn, and they sent for Zairong.
units.literal: That year on the last day of the intercalary seventh month, Li Jun and He Fujin together led the killing of the northern commander Mandale, seized the armory, the enemy's strength had not yet withdrawn, and Jun and the others sent men to summon Zairong.

units.zh: 再榮端坐本營，遲疑久之。
units.en: Zairong sat stiffly in his own camp, hesitating for a long while.
units.literal: Zairong sat upright in his own camp, hesitating for a long time.

units.zh: 為軍吏所迫，乃行。
units.en: Pressed by his officers, he finally went.
units.literal: Pressed by the army clerks, he then went.

units.zh: 翊日，逐出床答勒，諸軍以再榮名次在諸校之右，乃請權知留後事。
units.en: The next day they drove out Chuangdale. Because Zairong outranked the other commanders, the troops asked him to serve as acting regent.
units.literal: The next day they drove out Chuangdale; the armies, because Zairong's seniority ranked above the various commanders, then requested that he provisionally know regency affairs.

units.zh: 〈（《東都事略·李筠傳》：筠請馮道領節度，道曰：「予主奏事而已，留後事當議功臣為之。」
units.en: (《Eastern Capital Affairs Outline · Biography of Li Jun》: Jun asked Feng Dao to take the military commission. Dao said, "I am here only to handle memorials to the throne. The regency should go to a man of merit."
units.literal: (《Eastern Capital Affairs Outline · Biography of Li Jun》: Jun requested Feng Dao to take the military commission; Dao said: "I am in charge of memorializing affairs only; regency affairs should be discussed and given to a meritorious minister."

units.zh: 以諸將之甲者為留後。）〉
units.en: The commander with the highest rank was made regent.)〉
units.literal: The highest-ranked among the generals was made regent.)〉

units.zh: 再榮貪昧無決，舉止多疑，出入騎從，露刃註矢，諸校不相統攝，互有猜貳。
units.en: Zairong was greedy, indecisive, and suspicious. He went about surrounded by armed horsemen with blades drawn and bows strung. The commanders would not submit to one another and eyed each other with distrust.
units.literal: Zairong was greedy and dull without decision; his conduct was full of suspicion; going out and in he had mounted followers with bared blades and strung arrows; the various commanders did not command one another and mutually harbored doubt and division.

units.zh: 奉國廂主王饒懼為再榮所並，乃據東門樓，以兵自衛，偽稱足疾，不敢見再榮。
units.en: Wang Rao, commander of the Fengguo wing, feared that Zairong would swallow his command. He seized the east gate tower, garrisoned it with troops, feigned a foot ailment, and refused to see Zairong.
units.literal: Fengguo wing commander Wang Rao feared being absorbed by Zairong; he then held the east gate tower, used troops to protect himself, falsely claimed foot ailment, and did not dare see Zairong.

units.zh: 司天監趙延乂俱與之善，乃來往解釋，遂無相忌之意。
units.en: Zhao Yanyi of the Directorate of Astronomy was friendly with both men and shuttled between them until their mutual suspicion eased.
units.literal: Director of the Astronomy Bureau Zhao Yanyi was on good terms with both; he then went back and forth explaining, and thus there was no mutual suspicion.

units.zh: 再榮以李崧、和凝攜家在彼，令軍士數百人環迫崧、凝，以求賞給，崧、凝各出家財與之。
units.en: Because Li Song and He Ning had their families with them in the city, Zairong sent hundreds of soldiers to surround them and demand payment. Both men paid out of their private fortunes.
units.literal: Zairong, because Li Song and He Ning had brought their families there, ordered several hundred soldiers to surround and press Song and Ning to seek reward payments; Song and Ning each gave family wealth to them.

units.zh: 再榮欲害崧以利其財，前磁州刺史李穀謂再榮曰：「公與諸將為契丹所擄，淩辱萬端，旦夕憂死。
units.en: Zairong then planned to kill Song for his wealth. Li Gu, former prefect of Cizhou, said to him, "You and the other generals were captured by the Khitan, humiliated in every way, and lived in daily fear of death.
units.literal: Zairong wished to kill Song to profit from his wealth; former Cizhou prefect Li Gu said to Zairong: "You and the generals were captured by the Khitan, insulted in ten thousand ways, and feared death morning and evening.

units.zh: 今日眾力逐出蕃戎，鎮民死者不下三千人，豈獨公等之功！
units.en: Today the combined effort of many men drove out the barbarians, and no fewer than three thousand townspeople died. Was that victory yours alone!
units.literal: Today the multitude's strength drove out the barbarian forces; townspeople who died were not fewer than three thousand—how is it the achievement of you alone!

units.zh: 才得生路，便擬殺一宰相，他日到闕，儻有所問，何以為辭？」
units.en: You have only just won your lives, and already you would kill a chief minister. When you reach the capital, what answer will you give if you are questioned?"
units.literal: Just having gained a path to life, you now plan to kill a chief minister; when you reach the capital another day, if there should be questions, with what will you make your plea?"

units.zh: 再榮默然。
units.en: Zairong said nothing.
units.literal: Zairong was silent.

units.zh: 再榮又欲括率在城居民家財，以給軍士，李穀又譬解之，乃止。
units.en: Zairong next wanted to seize the property of everyone in the city to pay the troops, but Li Gu dissuaded him again and he desisted.
units.literal: Zairong again wished to assess and seize the household wealth of residents in the city to supply the soldiers; Li Gu again explained and dissuaded him, and he then stopped.

units.zh: 其漢人曾事滿達勒者盡拘之，以取其財。
units.en: He detained every Han who had once served Mandale and stripped them of their property.
units.literal: All Han people who had once served Mandale were detained to take their wealth.

units.zh: 高祖以再榮為鎮州留後，為政貪虐難狀，鎮人呼為「白麻答」。
units.en: Gaozu made Zairong regent of Zhenzhou. His rule was so greedy and cruel that the people called him "White Mandale."
units.literal: Gaozu made Zairong regent of Zhenzhou; his governance was greedy and cruel beyond description, and the people of the garrison called him "White Mandale."

units.zh: 未幾，移授滑州節度使，箕斂誅求，民不聊生，乃征還京師。
units.en: Soon he was transferred to Huazhou as military commissioner, where his crushing exactions left the people destitute. He was then recalled to the capital.
units.literal: Before long he was transferred and appointed military commissioner of Huazhou; he scraped together and demanded exactions, the people could not sustain life, and he was then summoned back to the capital.

units.zh: 周太祖入京城，軍士攻再榮之第，迫脅再榮，盡取財貨既，軍士前啟曰：「某等軍健，常趨事麾下，一旦無禮至此，今後何顏謁見？」
units.en: When Taizu of Zhou entered the capital, soldiers stormed Zairong's house and forced him to hand over everything he owned. Then one of them said, "We have always served under you, sir. After treating you so shamefully, how can we ever face you again?"
units.literal: When Zhou Taizu entered the capital, soldiers attacked Zairong's residence, coerced Zairong, and after completely taking his valuables, the soldiers stepped forward and said: "We soldiers have always hurried to serve under your command; suddenly to be discourteous to this extent—hereafter with what face shall we pay our respects?"

units.zh: 即奮刃擊之，挈其首而去，後家人以帛贖葬之。
units.en: They at once cut him down, took his head, and left. His family later ransomed the head with silk for burial.
units.literal: They then flourished blades and struck him, took his head and left; later his family used silk to ransom it for burial.

units.zh: 張鵬，鎮州鼓城人。
units.en: Zhang Peng was a native of Gucheng in Zhenzhou.
units.literal: Zhang Peng was a man of Gucheng in Zhenzhou.

units.zh: 幼為僧，知書，有口辯，喜大言，後歸俗。
units.en: As a boy he became a monk. He was literate, articulate, and fond of bold talk, and later returned to lay life.
units.literal: In youth he became a monk, knew books, had eloquence, delighted in grand speech, and later returned to lay life.

units.zh: 唐末帝為潞王時，鵬往依焉。
units.en: When the Last Emperor of Tang was still Prince of Lu, Peng went to serve him.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor of Tang was Prince of Lu, Peng went to rely on him.

units.zh: 及即位，用為供奉官，累監軍旅。
units.en: After his accession Peng was made a palace attendant and repeatedly supervised military affairs.
units.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, Peng was used as a palace attendant and repeatedly supervised armies.

units.zh: 晉開運中，契丹迫澶州，鵬為前鋒監押，奮身擊敵，被創而還。
units.en: During Jin Kaiyun, when the Khitan pressed Chanzhou, Peng served as vanguard overseer, charged the enemy at personal risk, was wounded, and withdrew.
units.literal: In Kaiyun of Jin the Khitan pressed Chanzhou; Peng was vanguard overseer, threw himself forward to strike the enemy, was wounded, and returned.

units.zh: 其後累於邊城戍守，士伍服其勇。
units.en: He later served repeatedly on frontier garrisons, and the troops respected his bravery.
units.literal: Thereafter he repeatedly garrisoned border cities, and the soldiers respected his courage.

units.zh: 乾祐初，授鎮州副使，過鄴城，高行周接之甚歡，鵬因言及晉朝傾亡之事，少帝任用失人，藩輔之臣，惟務積財富家，不以國家為意，以至宗社泯滅，非獨帝王之咎也。
units.en: Early in Qianyou he was made deputy commissioner of Zhenzhou. Passing through Yecheng he was warmly received by Gao Xingzhou, and Peng spoke of the fall of Jin: the Young Emperor had chosen the wrong men; frontier ministers cared only to enrich their families and not the state, until the dynasty was destroyed—a failure not of the emperor alone.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou he was appointed deputy commissioner of Zhenzhou. Passing through Yecheng, Gao Xingzhou received him very warmly, and Peng then spoke of the collapse of the Jin court: the Young Emperor employed the wrong men; the frontier ministers sought only to amass wealth for their families and did not care for the state, so that the altars of soil and grain were extinguished—not the fault of the emperor alone.

units.zh: 行周性寬和，不以鵬言為過。
units.en: Xingzhou was broad-minded and did not take Peng's remarks amiss.
units.literal: Xingzhou's nature was broad and mild; he did not regard Peng's words as a fault.

units.zh: 鵬既退，行周左右謂行周曰：「張副使之言，蓋譏令公也。」
units.en: After Peng left, Xingzhou's attendants said to him, "Deputy Commissioner Zhang's words were surely aimed at you, sir."
units.literal: After Peng had withdrawn, Xingzhou's attendants said to Xingzhou: "Deputy Commissioner Zhang's words surely mock Your Excellency."

units.zh: 行周因發怒，遂奏鵬怨國訛言，故朝廷降詔就誅於常山，時乾祐元年七月也。
units.en: Xingzhou then grew angry and memorialized that Peng had slandered the state out of resentment. The court issued an edict for his execution at Changshan, in the seventh month of Qianyou 1.
units.literal: Xingzhou thereupon grew angry and memorialized that Peng harbored resentment toward the state and spread slanderous talk; therefore the court issued an edict to execute him at Changshan. This was in the seventh month of the first year of Qianyou.

units.zh: 史臣曰：晉、漢之際，有以懋軍功、勤王事、取旌旄符竹者多矣，其間有及民之惠者無幾焉。
units.en: The historian writes: Between Jin and Han, many men won banners and provincial commands through military merit and loyal service to the throne, yet few of them brought any real benefit to the people.
units.literal: The historian says: In the transition between Jin and Han, many there were who through military achievement and diligent service to the throne obtained banners, staffs, and tally-bamboo posts, yet among them those who reached the people with kindness were few.

units.zh: 如王周之閫政、審交之民譽，蓋其優者也；
units.en: Men such as Wang Zhou in frontier administration and Liu Shenjiao in popular esteem were among the best;
units.literal: Such as Wang Zhou's border governance and Shenjiao's popular reputation—these were roughly the superior ones;

units.zh: 漢球、張瓘抑又次焉。
units.en: while Hanqiu and Zhang Guan ranked a step below them.
units.literal: Hanqiu and Zhang Guan were again a step below.

units.zh: 是宜紀之篇以示來者，其餘皆不足觀也已。
units.en: These are the men worth recording for posterity; the rest are scarcely worth notice.
units.literal: Therefore they are fit to be recorded in chapters to show those who come after; the rest are not worth viewing.

units.zh: 張鵬以一言之失，遽滅其身，亦足誡後代多言橫議之徒歟！
units.en: Zhang Peng destroyed himself over a single ill-chosen remark—a warning, too, for later generations of men who talk too much and argue too freely!
units.literal: Zhang Peng through one slip of speech suddenly destroyed his person—this is also enough to admonish later generations' crowd of much talk and reckless discussion!

findings.action: Retain the transfer and source wording but remove the unsupported fixed interval; use an explicitly qualified unresolved or one-sided chronology only if independently evidenced.

findings.action: Remove the inferred maternal activity range and hint while preserving the source-backed mother relationship.

findings.action: Correct all Tang Tianyou intervals and matching hints to the verified AD 904–907 era bounds, retaining source wording and persons.

findings.action: Remove the unsupported temporal attestation and active-date hint; retain the cited warning and identity evidence.
